response:
It makes complete sense that being treated poorly has left a mark—those wounds don't heal overnight, and the fact that you're ready to move forward shows real strength.

A few things that can help: start noticing the harsh things you say to yourself and gently challenge them, like you would question an unfair comment from someone else. Reconnect with activities and people who remind you of who you are outside that relationship. And when the overthinking spirals, try grounding yourself in the present—your mind often replays the past to try to "solve" pain, but you don't owe those memories more of your time. Small, consistent acts of self-kindness rebuild self-worth more than any single big step.

If these feelings become overwhelming or persistent, talking with a therapist can be really valuable—they can help you process what happened and rebuild at your own pace. You deserved better than how you were treated, and you're worth the effort you're putting in now.
